body:
## Bottom line

**Recommendation (Large effort): build a capability-separated, two-site architecture with a server-side publication data diode.** The Audience application must be treated as hostile/public: it cannot receive, address, cache, or derive any Presenter, transcript, RAG-candidate, ACL, or team-message data. Prefer different registrable domains (not merely sibling subdomains), same-origin WSS on each site, opaque role-specific sessions, and an immutable server-built `PublishedAudienceCard` as the only datum crossing private -> public.

The greenfield claim “separate routes plus server permissions” is insufficient. A hidden panel, client-side filtering, encrypted private payload, shared event stream, BroadcastChannel, shared service worker, shared JWT, or post-filtered vector results all violate the boundary.

### Reference topology

```text
PRIVATE PLANE
Console site + paired device -> Console Gateway/WSS -> Orchestrator
                                             |-> transcript/audio jobs
                                             |-> ACL-filtered retrieval/source store
                                             |-> untrusted LLM Candidate
                                             `-> rights/privacy/support verifier
                                                        |
                                                  Publish Gate
                                                        | immutable allowlisted DTO only
PUBLIC PLANE                                            v
Audience site/WSS <- Audience Gateway <- published_cards store/topic
```

Audience Gateway has no credential or network path to the private stores/event bus. This architectural non-reachability is stronger than runtime filtering.

## Action plan

1. **Create browser/security boundaries first.** Host Console and Audience on separate registrable domains where feasible. Use distinct builds, manifests, service workers, cookies, APIs, WSS namespaces, CSPs, and deploy identities. Audience gets no CORS/private API connectivity, no third-party JS, and `Permissions-Policy` denying microphone/camera/display-capture/notifications. Console private responses are `Cache-Control: no-store`; store no sensitive content/token in Cache API, IndexedDB, localStorage, URL, logs, or crash analytics.

2. **Implement a one-way publish state machine.** `candidate -> supported -> rights_verified -> privacy_approved -> presenter_approved -> published -> expired/revoked`. `SUPPORTED` alone never publishes. The client/model sends only `candidate_id`; a server builder emits a closed-schema immutable DTO (`additionalProperties:false`) containing plain text, approved asset hash, public citations/attribution, alt text, and expiry. Unknown/internal/HTML fields fail closed. Internal-RAG cards require manual approval; fast auto-publish is limited to pre-approved public corpora and deterministic templates.

3. **Preserve extended-display UX without weakening isolation.** Console requests Window Management permission, then a fresh user click calls cross-origin `window.open()` with target-screen geometry, `noopener,noreferrer`. Audience needs its own click for fullscreen. Both sites use `COOP: same-origin`; accept losing useful WindowProxy access and replace `.closed/focus/close` with server-mediated WSS `ready/heartbeat/close`. Window Management is limited/experimental, so manual drag/fullscreen is mandatory. Screen topology changes trigger a privacy curtain and re-confirmation. In mirrored mode, the presentation PC runs Audience only; Console runs on a paired personal device.

4. **Issue independent opaque sessions/capabilities.** Separate Account, PresentationControl, Device, and AudienceDisplay sessions, each 128-bit+ opaque server-side ID in host-only `__Host-` Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict cookies. Rotate at login, presentation start, pairing, role change and handoff; revoke and close sockets at session end. Exact `Origin` + CSRF token are mandatory: sibling subdomains are same-site, so SameSite and `Sec-Fetch-Site` cannot stop sibling-origin CSRF. WSS subscriptions come from the server principal; never accept arbitrary room/topic or query-string auth.

5. **Pair devices as approval transactions, never QR bearer login.** Existing private Console creates a one-use 90s pending transaction; QR carries only a high-entropy correlation value. New device authenticates, both devices display the same short authentication string, and existing Console approves device name + exact scopes. Five failed attempts terminate the transaction. Approval consumes it and creates a new presentation-scoped DeviceSession. List/revoke active devices. Mutations require primary-controller lease, `controller_epoch`, monotonic sequence, and idempotency key; stale controller/duplicate/out-of-order commands reject.

6. **Put authorization around RAG, not inside the LLM/vector result.** Server derives tenant/subject/groups/clearance/purpose/policy version. Tenant partition and ABAC/ReBAC metadata filter execute before ANN/top-k; policy post-authorizes every object. Reauthorize when materializing bytes and immediately before publication against current ACL, exact revision, and content hash. Policy unavailable/stale/missing metadata returns zero. Cache keys include tenant + authorization fingerprint + policy/corpus revision. Presenter-readable never implies audience-publishable. Retrieved content is hostile data: it cannot change tools, filters, URLs, policy, or publish state.

7. **Make audio capture revocable and deletion provable.** Browser mic permission is not legal consent. Before capture, show controller/purposes/vendors/region/retention/withdrawal notice and record policy-version acknowledgment or configured lawful basis. Ingest accepts frames only under a short-lived CaptureGrant. On stop, end, logout, revoke, or control-channel loss: stop every MediaStreamTrack, close uploader/vendor job, revoke grant; ingest drops the next frame. Raw PCM is memory-only (recommended <=30s retry ring). Attach deletion TTL at creation; cascade deletion through queue, provider, transcript, embeddings, prompts/cache, reports/exports/analytics. Use per-session encryption keys, backup tombstones, provider acknowledgments, and never report success while any store is pending. Legal holds are reasoned, expiring, narrowly ACL'd, and visibly disclosed.

8. **Make rights metadata executable policy.** Every public asset hash needs a RightsRecord: canonical source, creator/title/holder, license ID/version/URL or grant, captured evidence, commercial/adaptation conditions, attribution, territory/expiry, releases, and exact bytes hash. Unknown/all-rights-reserved/ambiguous remains a private link. Enforce CC/public-domain conditions; generated assets still need terms/version/input/person/brand review. Do not hotlink. Fetch through SSRF-isolated egress, reject private/link-local/metadata IP before and after redirects, bound bytes/time/pixels, reject SVG for MVP, safe raster re-encode, strip sensitive EXIF, and self-host immutable bytes. C2PA proves provenance/integrity, not permission. Index asset hash -> all cards for instant takedown.

9. **Ship release-blocking adversarial tests, not policy prose.** Target OWASP ASVS Level 2. Automate the gates below and exercise the real extended and mirrored workflows before pilot.

## Enforceable cross-boundary invariants

- **INV-01 Noninterference:** every Audience-observable byte is a function only of published DTOs and public display state.
- **INV-02 Non-reachability:** Audience deployment identity/network ACL cannot read private databases, buckets, queues, topics, KMS keys, or vendor jobs.
- **INV-03 One-way transition:** only Publish Gate writes `published_cards`; Console, LLM, search and Audience cannot.
- **INV-04 Closed public schema:** unknown field, HTML/Markdown, internal URI/ID, transcript, prompt/query, ACL/classification, speaker/team/provider/debug metadata => reject.
- **INV-05 Fail private:** missing/stale ACL, rights, revision/hash, policy, consent/lawful-basis config, deletion acknowledgment, or classification => no disclosure.
- **INV-06 Separate authority:** read permission, evidence support, privacy clearance, rights clearance, and audience publish permission are independent predicates.
- **INV-07 Per-message auth:** every HTTP/WSS command is authorized at use time; handshake auth or possession of room ID is never sufficient.
- **INV-08 Single controller:** exactly one controller epoch can mutate a presentation; handoff atomically invalidates the old epoch/sockets.
- **INV-09 No reusable pairing secret:** observed QR/code cannot yield a session without authenticated-device confirmation and explicit approval.
- **INV-10 Capture revocation:** after CaptureGrant revocation time, zero subsequent audio frames are accepted, including queued/retried frames.
- **INV-11 Deletion completeness:** deletion is successful only when all online stores/providers acknowledge and restore tests prove tombstones reapply to backups.
- **INV-12 Rights bind bytes:** approval applies to a content hash, use context and license evidence—not a mutable URL or search label.
- **INV-13 Topology distrust:** browser screen placement is convenience, never proof of privacy; any topology uncertainty curtains private UI.
- **INV-14 No secret persistence:** credentials/private content never enter URL/history, browser web storage/cache, audience SW, referrer, notifications, logs, replay/APM screenshots, or analytics.

## Release-blocking evidence

- Inspect Audience packets, reconnect snapshot, DOM, JS bundle, SW/cache/storage and logs: no private field/event/token exists.
- Cross-tenant/group-denied retrieval returns zero; revoked ACL between retrieval/render rejects; cache cannot replay another principal; policy outage fails closed.
- Poisoned document/search result cannot choose tools/URL/topic or advance publication; XSS payload renders inert text.
- Malicious WSS Origin, cross-site POST, arbitrary topic, expired/rotated cookie, Audience publish command, stale controller and duplicate sequence all reject.
- QR screenshot, brute force, replay after use/expiry and revoked device cannot connect/control.
- Unknown license, commercial use of NC, modified ND, missing attribution, changed URL bytes and redirect-to-private-IP all reject.
- No grant audio rejects; midstream revoke drops next frame; durable raw audio/log scan is empty; provider closes; deletion removes transcript/vector/cache/report and remains removed after backup restore.
- Screen removal/current-screen change curtains Console before next private payload; mirrored-machine browser profile has no Console cookie; emergency unpublish reaches every Audience connection and reconnect snapshot.

## Risks and mitigations

- **OS mirroring/recording/shoulder surfing cannot be detected reliably by a PWA.** Mitigation: paired personal-device Console is the high-confidentiality mode; extended mode uses explicit placement check/curtain only.
- **Window Management and programmatic fullscreen are permissioned, limited and browser-dependent.** Mitigation: two-step user gesture plus manual drag/fullscreen fallback; never couple security to placement success.
- **Separate registrable domains add deployment/SSO complexity.** Mitigation: same backend identity provider with audience never receiving AccountSession; separate reverse-proxied WSS and CI policy tests. If sibling subdomains must be used, exact Origin + CSRF are absolute requirements.
- **DLP is probabilistic and copyright/privacy law is jurisdiction/context-specific.** Mitigation: DLP is supplemental to deterministic classification/rights records and manual approval; obtain Korean/privacy/IP counsel before pilot and encode the approved policy version.
- **Provider deletion/no-training promises are contractual, not technical.** Mitigation: vendor due diligence, regional endpoint, retention-off configuration, deletion API/receipts, subprocessor inventory and periodic restore/deletion drills.
- **A compromised Console can publish allowed-looking misinformation.** Mitigation: CSP/no third-party JS, candidate-only publish commands, server reconstruction/verifiers, single-controller lease, audit trail and emergency revoke; use step-up auth for high-impact sessions.

## Primary sources

- NIST Zero Trust SP 800-207: https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/207/final
- MDN Window Management, postMessage/BroadcastChannel, COOP, cookies, Fetch Metadata, Cache-Control/Clear-Site-Data, Permissions Policy and MediaStreamTrack.stop: https://developer.mozilla.org/
